summary: In this excerpt from Book 10, the narrator, left alone in his office and nominally in charge after Rhindquist leaves, explores the company's personnel files on the office TV. He reads his own file, his mother's, family records, and Buddy's, and finds that the Security Manager who had Buddy locked up was engaged to Carla, Buddy's wife and the Security Manager's ex-girlfriend. The narrator uses his access to free Buddy and Carla, promote them, and demote the Security Manager to janitor, and he also sets up his friends back home. Tony brings sorted boxes of documents at lunch, and the chapter ends with an angry caller demanding McBride, and the narrator, filling in, feeling sick.
one_line: A young office worker, briefly in charge, uses company personnel files to free and promote his brother-in-law and sister-in-law, then faces an angry caller.
key_facts: Tony is ordered to go to the third floor, sort the shredded material, box it, and have it on the narrator's desk by lunch.
Rhindquist tells the narrator, "Sonny-boy, you're going to do just fine."
The narrator opens the personnel files on the office TV and finds his own file goes back to the Infirmary where he was born.
The narrator finds that Mom had her tubes tied, which he did not know.
Buddy's personnel file is spotless until the spying accusation.
The Security Manager who "caught" Buddy was engaged to Carla last year, and Carla is Buddy's ex-girlfriend.
Buddy and Carla are married, and Carla's ex-boyfriend, the Security Manager, had them locked up.
The narrator gets Buddy and Carla out of jail, gives them promotions, and has the Security Manager busted down to a janitor.
The narrator says it scares him to have that much power but it feels good too.
Tony returns at lunchtime with three big boxes of papers sorted into memos, personal documents and inter-departmental communications.
The narrator compares himself to the queen ant sitting in the middle of the hill watching the drones.
The narrator answers the phone as "Jasper Whitehead, Special Vice-President."
The caller shouts, "Get me McBride, now!"
The narrator says McBride is not available and that he is filling in for him.
